findings.evidence: The request concerns preventing tests from writing to `logs/usage/` and explicitly scopes product-recording changes out; it says nothing about release artifacts. Nevertheless `required_outputs` requires `releases/_next/tests-never-write-usage-log.md`, `release-note-present-and-shaped` gates its structure, and `release-note-accurate` prescribes its prose. The cited “Delivery contract (`.method.yaml` delivery, `releases/README.md`, `pr-checks.yml`)” is not among the selected pinned definitions.
findings.summary: The contract requires a release note and prescribes its contents even though neither the request nor any pinned definition requires one.

findings.evidence: The request requires that running all of `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` leave every file under `logs/usage/` unchanged and create no new file. But `scope-is-the-file-list` says the permitted change set is exactly the enumerated files, while `gap-writers-inferred` admits that the writer list is only inferred and says a writer outside those files merely becomes “a scope defect.” The request requires such a writer to be redirected or stopped, so the contract cannot both forbid editing its module and require the suite-wide outcome.
findings.summary: The exact permitted-file restriction can prevent fixing a real test writer, contradicting the request’s suite-wide outcome.

findings.evidence: `live-tier-consistent` requires that “A manual paid run is not stopped by the guard and records into a temporary directory,” and `decision-live-tier-usage` likewise requires paid live-tier runs to record there. The only dedicated deterministic criterion, `live-tier-still-collects`, runs `pytest tests/live --collect-only`; its own expected text says “Nothing is run.” `full-test-suite` excludes live tests through the unchanged `pytest.ini` marker configuration. Thus the checks can pass even if an executed live test is stopped by the guard or writes no temporary usage record.
findings.summary: The contract claims manual live tests record successfully into a temporary directory, but its checks only collect those tests and never exercise that behavior.

summary: The core guard and base-failure demonstration are substantially covered, but the contract adds an unsupported release-note deliverable, restricts fixes so undiscovered writers may remain unfixed, and does not behaviorally verify its live-tier recording guarantee.
